questions.text: Alan Turing is one of the most notable LGBTQ+ scientists from history. Which German code did his machine, the Bombe, help to break?
questions.funfact: 💻 Turing's Bombe machine is estimated to have shortened World War II by 2-4 years, saving millions of lives. Tragically, Turing was later persecuted for his homosexuality and died in 1954 — he received a posthumous royal pardon in 2013.

questions.text: In which city did the Rainbow Pride flag originate in 1978?
questions.funfact: 🏳️‍🌈 The flag was created by artist Gilbert Baker for San Francisco's Gay Freedom Day parade. The original flag had 8 colours, but two were dropped due to fabric availability, leaving the now-iconic 6-stripe design.

questions.text: In what year was Call Me By Your Name released, did Dua Lipa release 'New Rules', and did Australia legalise same-sex marriage? (Year Format: YYYY)
questions.funfact: 🏳️‍🌈 Australia's same-sex marriage law passed with overwhelming public support — a national postal survey showed 61.6% in favour before parliament voted to legalise it in December 2017.

questions.text: In the song and organisation YMCA, what does the C stand for?
questions.funfact: 🏳️‍🌈 YMCA stands for Young Men's Christian Association, founded in London in 1844. The Village People's 1978 song of the same name has since become an enduring gay anthem, despite the band always denying any explicit LGBTQ+ meaning.

questions.text: In Gen Z slang, what does 'slay' mean?
options: To excel or succeed with style and confidence
questions.funfact: 💅 'Slay' has roots in Black and ballroom culture dating back decades before going mainstream — ballroom culture, pioneered by LGBTQ+ communities of colour in the 1980s, has heavily influenced modern internet slang.

questions.text: Queen Elizabeth II was famous for owning which breed of dog?
questions.funfact: 🐕 The Queen owned over 30 corgis during her reign, all descended from her first corgi Susan, gifted to her on her 18th birthday in 1944.

questions.text: Who wrote 'The Picture of Dorian Gray'?
questions.funfact: 📖 Oscar Wilde was later imprisoned for 'gross indecency' due to his relationships with men — a conviction that destroyed his career and health. He was given a posthumous pardon by the UK government in 2017.

questions.text: Name ABBA's top 5 most streamed songs on Spotify (1 point each)
answers: lay all your love on me
acceptedAnswers: lay all your love on me
questions.funfact: 💃 Dancing Queen is ABBA's most streamed song with over 2 billion streams — it was written specifically to be performed at the wedding of King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden in 1976.

questions.text: 'I Will Survive' wins the first and last Grammy ever awarded for Best Disco Recording. Who was the artist?
questions.funfact: 🪩 The Best Disco Recording category was created and retired in the same year — 1980 — after backlash against disco's mainstream dominance. Gaynor's hit has since become a global gay-rights anthem covered in over 20 languages.

questions.text: Complete the next five words: 'I'm never gonna dance again, guilty feet have got no rhythm, though it's easy to pretend, I —'
questions.funfact: 🎶 This is from 'Careless Whisper' by George Michael — co-written when he was just 17, it became one of the best-selling singles of all time, with over 6 million UK certified sales alone.

questions.text: What movie did Tom Hanks win his first Best Actor Oscar for, playing a gay lawyer with AIDS?
questions.funfact: Many of the courtroom extras were real people living with HIV/AIDS, recruited through the Philadelphia support group ActionAIDS.

questions.text: What does 'Mardi Gras' mean in French?
questions.funfact: 🎭 Mardi Gras gets its name because it's the last day to indulge in rich, fatty foods before the fasting period of Lent begins on Ash Wednesday.

questions.text: Who has more US Billboard Hot 100 #1 hits — Elton John or Queen?
questions.funfact: 🎹 Elton John has 9 US #1 hits including 'Candle in the Wind 1997' and 'That's What Friends Are For'. Queen only managed 2 — 'Crazy Little Thing Called Love' and 'Another One Bites the Dust'. Surprisingly, 'Bohemian Rhapsody' never hit #1 in the US, peaking at #2.

questions.text: What dance was performed in 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show'?
questions.funfact: 🎬 The term 'Easter Egg' is said to have originated from this movie — the cast supposedly left actual Easter eggs lying around on set, and spotting them in the finished film became a fun tradition for fans.

questions.text: What word can fill in the blank: '_s of the Stone Age', '_ of Hearts' and 'Priscilla, _ of the Desert'?
questions.funfact: 🎬 'The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert' (1994) became a landmark LGBTQ+ film, later adapted into a hit stage musical that has toured the world.

questions.text: Which famous fashion designer has also directed Oscar-nominated movies such as 'Nocturnal Animals' and 'A Single Man'?
questions.funfact: 🎬 Before becoming a director, Tom Ford spent a decade as creative director of Gucci and Yves Saint Laurent.

questions.text: The first openly gay prime minister, Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir, hailed from which country?
questions.shoutout: 🙌 Big shoutout to Talisia for this question!
questions.funfact: 🇮🇸 Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir served as Iceland's Prime Minister from 2009 to 2013, becoming the world's first openly lesbian head of government in modern history.

questions.text: In old Nokia phone keypad language (T9 texting), what does the following translate as: 44 2 7 7 999 0 7 777 444 3 33?
questions.funfact: 📱 Old Nokia phones used T9 predictive text where each number key represented 3-4 letters texting fluently on these keypads was practically a rite of passage for anyone who grew up in the 2000s!

weekly_quizzes.title: Big Fat Sunday Quiz #11
weekly_quizzes.description: Bens Trivia is proudly partnering up with Windsor Bowls Club in Brisbane Australia, the very first venue to get Bens Trivia Coasters! 🙌 Big Shoutout to Windsor Bowls Club!

questions.text: Which film contains the line - Life moves pretty fast. If you don't stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.
questions.funfact: The line is from Ferris Bueller's Day Off (1986), the script was famously written by John Hughes in just six days.

questions.text: Which player has just broken the all-time record for most goals scored at FIFA World Cups?
questions.funfact: Messi broke Miroslav Klose's long-standing record of 16 goals during the 2026 World Cup, becoming the tournament's all-time top scorer.

questions.text: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, which word represents the letter Q?
questions.funfact: Quebec is also the only NATO phonetic alphabet word named after a place rather than a generic word.

questions.text: Which country will host both the 2027 Rugby World Cup and the 2032 Olympics?
questions.funfact: Brisbane will specifically host the 2032 Olympics, while the Rugby World Cup matches will be spread across multiple Australian cities.

questions.text: Which singer is an anagram of VERILY SLEEPS?
questions.funfact: Elvis Presley is often called 'The King of Rock and Roll' and remains one of the best-selling solo artists in history.

questions.text: Sumo wrestling has deep ceremonial ties to which religion?
questions.funfact: Many sumo rituals, like the purification of the ring with salt, come directly from Shinto practices.

questions.text: Caitlyn Jenner (formerly known as Bruce Jenner) won Olympic gold in 1976. Which event did she compete in?
questions.funfact: Jenner set a world record of 8,618 points winning the decathlon at the 1976 Montreal Olympics, earning the unofficial title of 'world's greatest athlete'.

questions.text: Which letter of the alphabet do the most chemical elements begin with?
questions.funfact: 12 elements start with C including Carbon, Calcium, Chromium, Copper, Caesium, and Curium more than any other letter.

questions.text: The surname Kim is most commonly found in which country?
questions.funfact: About 1 in 5 South Koreans and 1 in 4 North Koreans are named Kim, making it one of the most concentrated surnames in the world.

questions.text: In which year did Princess Diana die, the Spice Girls release 'Wannabe', and Good Will Hunting come out?
questions.funfact: Princess Diana's death in August 1997 became one of the most-watched news events in history.

questions.text: In corporate/business language, what does the acronym ICT stand for?
questions.funfact: ICT is often used instead of just 'IT' to emphasise the role of communications (like networks and telecoms) alongside computing.

questions.text: Finish the saying: "It's better to light a candle than to curse the..."
questions.funfact: While often misattributed to ancient Chinese philosophy or Eleanor Roosevelt, the phrase was actually coined by English Methodist preacher William Lonsdale Watkinson in a 1907 sermon.

questions.text: Which country is widely ranked as having the fastest average internet speed in the world?
questions.funfact: Singapore has topped global broadband speed rankings for several years running, thanks to its dense fibre infrastructure.

questions.text: Which of these happened first?
questions.funfact: Captain Cook reached Australia's east coast in 1770, the US declared independence in 1776, the French Revolution began in 1789, and the Irish Famine started in 1845.

questions.text: 2 of the 7 Wonders of the (Modern) World are Petra and Chichen Itza. Name the other 5 (hint: their countries start with C, B, P, I, and I).
questions.funfact: These are the New7Wonders of the World, chosen by a global public poll in 2007. The Great Pyramid of Giza, the only surviving wonder of the ancient world, wasn't part of the vote but was given honorary 8th-wonder status.

questions.text: What was the title of Adele's first studio album? (Hint: A number)
questions.funfact: Released in 2008, 19 was named for Adele's age while writing most of its songs, a naming convention she repeated with 21, 25, and 30.

questions.text: What are the next 5 lyrics? - I don't wanna close my eyes, I don't wanna fall asleep, 'Cause I'd miss you baby, And I don't wanna miss a thing, 'Cause even when I dream of you, The _
questions.funfact: It was Aerosmith's only number-one single on the Billboard Hot 100, and was written by Diane Warren specifically for the film Armageddon.

questions.text: Besides the 4 species of echidna, there's only one other mammal that lays eggs. What is it?
questions.funfact: Echidnas and platypuses together make up the monotremes, the only mammals that lay eggs instead of giving birth to live young.

questions.text: What is the name of the man on the KFC logo?
questions.funfact: Sanders made surprise visits to KFC restaurants and frequently complained to the press about the food quality. He famously called their newly formulated gravy 'wallpaper paste' and 'sludge'.

questions.text: Which is taller: the Eiffel Tower or the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
questions.funfact: The Eiffel Tower stands about 330 metres tall, while the Leaning Tower of Pisa is only around 56 metres, the Eiffel Tower is roughly six times taller.

questions.text: What does a phycologist study (not to be confused with a psychologist)?
questions.funfact: Phycology and psychology sound almost identical, but a phycologist studies algae and seaweed, while a psychologist studies the mind and behavior.

questions.text: What single word can go before 'hold', before 'rail', and after 'before'?
questions.funfact: That gives you 'handhold', 'handrail', and 'beforehand'.

questions.text: Nickelback, Voting, and Silverback all share a common link. Which of these words can also be included?
questions.funfact: All of these words contain an element from the pariodic table. Bandleader hides (lead) joining nickelback (nickel), voting (tin), and silverback (silver) as another word with a chemical element hidden inside.

questions.text: Dave Dobbyn's 'Slice of Heaven' (with Herbs) was written for which 1986 New Zealand film?
questions.shoutout: 🙌 Shoutout to Danielle for this one!
questions.funfact: The song went on to spend 8 weeks at number one in New Zealand. It was often used in TV ads to encourage people to visit New Zealand.

questions.text: How many possible opening moves does White have on the very first move of a chess game?
questions.funfact: Each of White's 8 pawns can move 1 or 2 squares (16 options), plus each of the 2 knights has 2 possible moves (4 options) giving 20 total.

questions.text: Which film features the line 'You had me at hello'?
questions.funfact: The line was reportedly improvised by Renee Zellweger during filming and wasn't in the original script.

questions.text: Which tennis legend, aged 44, made a surprise return to Wimbledon 2026 only to be knocked out in the first round by Australian Maya Joint?
questions.funfact: Her first singles Grand Slam match in nearly four years since the 2022 US Open. The 23-time Grand Slam champion returned to the court as a mother of two, having given birth to daughter Olympia in 2017 and a second daughter Adira in 2023.

questions.text: Out of these Italian phrases - which of these is NOT a way to say goodbye?
questions.funfact: Ciao works for both hello and goodbye informally, Arrivederci is the formal farewell, and Addio is a dramatic final goodbye where as Salute means 'cheers' or 'bless you', not goodbye.

questions.text: On what date does France celebrate Bastille Day?
questions.funfact: Bastille Day marks the storming of the Bastille prison on 14 July 1789, a key event of the French Revolution. The other dates are all national celebrations too. 4th July is American Independence Day, 12th July is Orange Day in Northern Ireland, and 21st July is Belgian National Day.

questions.text: Which actress is an anagram of TRY EEL SPERM?
questions.funfact: Meryl Streep holds the record for the most acting Oscar nominations (21) and has won three times.

questions.text: What is the traditional garnish for an Old Fashioned cocktail?
questions.funfact: A maraschino cherry is sometimes added too, but the orange peel (twisted to release its oils) is considered the classic garnish.

questions.text: What colour is most associated with the company Tiffany & Co.?
questions.funfact: Tiffany Blue has been a registered trademark colour since 1998 and is officially known as Pantone 1837, named after Tiffany's founding year.

questions.text: Which of the following is the most lethal by gram?
questions.funfact: Apple seeds contain amygdalin, a natural compound of cyanide and sugar. You would have to meticulously chew and crush anywhere from 150 to several thousand seeds in one sitting to be at risk.

questions.text: Which is the only country in the world whose name ends with the letter H?
questions.funfact: Bangladesh is the only country whose English name ends in 'h'.

questions.text: In which year did Martin Luther King Jr. deliver his 'I Have a Dream' speech, JFK get assassinated, and The Beatles release their first album 'Please Please Me'?
questions.funfact: All three events happened within months of each other in 1963, a hugely consequential year in world history.

questions.text: What does the 'M' stand for in GMT (Londons Timezone)?
questions.funfact: GMT (Greenwich Mean Time)is based on the mean solar time at the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London, and was historically used as the basis for world time zones.

questions.text: Finish the phrase: 'Lions for...'
questions.funfact: Lions for Lambs is an idiom describing a scenario where brave, capable individuals (the lions) are sacrificed, exploited, or led to their doom by incompetent or selfish leaders (the lambs); 'Lions for Lambs' is also the title of a 2007 film starring Tom Cruise, Robert Redford and Meryl Streep.

questions.text: What is the name for fermented honey, often considered one of the oldest alcoholic drinks in the world?
questions.funfact: Mead is made by fermenting honey with water and is sometimes called 'honey wine', despite not using grapes.

questions.text: Which of these gods came first?
questions.funfact: Ra was worshipped in ancient Egypt from at least 2600 BCE. For comparison, Buddha lived around the 5th century BC, Jesus around 4BC - 30AD, and Muhammad around 570–632 AD making Ra one of the oldest major gods still widely known today

questions.text: According to Wikipedia: Name the top 5 countries by tea consumption per capita. (Hint: India or China are not on the list!)
questions.funfact: Turkey tops global per-capita tea consumption, with the average Turk drinking several cups a day. Azerbaijan, Ireland and the UK are not far behind, tea is deeply embedded in all three cultures.

questions.text: Who originally wrote 'Make You Feel My Love', later made famous by Adele?
questions.funfact: Dylan wrote it for his 1997 album Time Out of Mind. Billy Joel actually released his own cover first, two months before Dylan's version came out, but Dylan wrote the song.

questions.text: What are the next 5 lyrics - Sweet Dreams Are Made of these_
questions.funfact: The song, by Eurythmics, was released in 1983 and became one of the most recognisable synth-pop tracks of the decade.

questions.text: Hippos famously secrete a thick, oily red fluid sometimes called 'blood sweat'. What is its actual purpose?
questions.funfact: The secretion starts clear, turns red then brown, and acts as a natural sunscreen, moisturiser and antibiotic. Hippos don't actually have sweat glands.

questions.text: Which of these franchises does NOT feature Jack Black?
questions.funfact: Jack Black voices Po in Kung Fu Panda, Bowser in The Super Mario Bros. Movie, and plays Steve in A Minecraft Movie but has no role in How to Train Your Dragon.

questions.text: Which has more bones: an adult cat or an adult human?
questions.funfact: Cats have around 230 bones compared to a human's 206 the extra bones come mainly from their flexible spine and long tail.

questions.text: Why was the world's first webcam created, back in 1991?
options: To monitor a server room's temperature
To check if a coffee pot was full
For a university's CCTV security system
questions.funfact: Researchers at Cambridge University's Computer Lab set up a camera pointed at their coffee pot so they wouldn't waste a trip to find it empty.

questions.text: Which organ is affected by cirrhosis?
questions.funfact: The liver is the body’s largest internal organ and a true metabolic powerhouse. Performing over 500 essential functions, it acts as your personal filtration system, nutrient processor, and energy storage hub—all while holding the unique superpower of being able to completely regenerate itself after injury

questions.text: What letter can replace the question mark to complete the sequence: SG, SR, AN, W?
questions.funfact: Each pair is the first and last letter of a season: SprinG, SummeR, AutumN, WinteR.

questions.text: Which is the smallest planet in our solar system?
questions.funfact: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system about 38% the size of Earth. Despite being closest to the Sun, it's not the hottest planet that title belongs to Venus.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Jarrod for this question!

questions.text: What is 20% of 20% of 20?
questions.funfact: 20% of 20 is 4, and 20% of 4 is 0.8

questions.text: Which film features the iconic line: 'I'm mad as hell, and I'm not going to take it anymore!'?
questions.funfact: The line is delivered by news anchor Howard Beale in the 1976 film Network, directed by Sidney Lumet. It was voted #19 on the AFI's 100 greatest movie quotes list.

questions.text: Which horror film has been the biggest box office hit of 2026, grossing over $300 US million worldwide?
questions.funfact: Obsession, directed by YouTuber-turned-filmmaker Curry Barker, was made for under $1 million and grossed over $370 million worldwide one of the most profitable films ever made.

questions.text: Which country has the highest linguistic diversity in the world, with over 800 languages spoken?
questions.funfact: Papua New Guinea boasts over 800 distinct languages despite its relatively small population a result of its mountainous terrain and historically isolated tribal communities.

questions.text: Which of these music festivals attracts the most attendees?
questions.funfact: Sziget in Budapest draws around 420,000–500,000 attendees over seven days ahead of Tomorrowland (~400,000), Glastonbury (~210,000), and Coachella (~125,000 per weekend). Glastonbury also takes a fallow year in 2026.

questions.text: Unscramble this anagram to find a country: HAIL UNITA
questions.funfact: Lithuania is one of the three Baltic states and was the first Soviet republic to declare independence in 1990.

questions.text: What is the main ingredient in the traditional South Asian dish dal?
questions.funfact: Dal refers both to dried split legumes and the warmly spiced stew made from them. Red lentils, yellow lentils, mung beans and pigeon peas are all common varieties.

questions.text: Which celebrity founded the Fenty brand?
questions.funfact: Rihanna launched Fenty Beauty in 2017 to widespread acclaim for its 40-shade foundation range, making her one of the wealthiest female musicians in the world.

questions.text: On the colour wheel, what colour is directly opposite yellow?
questions.funfact: Purple sits directly opposite yellow on the colour wheel, making them complementary colours. When placed next to each other, complementary colours create the strongest visual contrast.

questions.text: What was New York City originally called before being renamed by the English in 1664?
questions.funfact: New Amsterdam was the Dutch colonial settlement founded at the southern tip of Manhattan in 1626. The English seized it in 1664 and renamed it New York after the Duke of York.

questions.text: In what year did the Chernobyl disaster happen, was Top Gun released in cinemas, and Bon Jovi release Livin' on a Prayer?
questions.funfact: 1986 was quite a year the Chernobyl nuclear disaster in April, Top Gun topping the box office, and Livin' on a Prayer becoming one of the best-selling singles of all time.

questions.text: What does the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Z do on a computer?
questions.funfact: Ctrl+Z is the universal undo shortcut, originally introduced by Apple in the early 1980s. The Z was chosen simply because it was close to Ctrl on the keyboard not for any specific meaning.

questions.text: In Gen Z slang, what does 'no cap' mean?
questions.funfact: 'No cap' means 'no lie' or 'I'm being completely serious.' The opposite, 'capping,' means lying or exaggerating. It was cemented in the rap lexicon by tracks such as Young Thug and Future's 2017 song No Cap and Lil Baby's 2018 track No Cap and went mainstream via social media around 2018.

questions.text: In which country did Tarot cards originate?
questions.funfact: Tarot cards originated in northern Italy in the 15th century as playing cards. They weren't widely used for fortune-telling until the late 18th century in France.

questions.text: In which modern-day country is beer thought to have first been made, around 8,000 BC?
questions.funfact: Beer is thought to have been invented by the Sumerians in what is now Iraq around 8,000 BC. Ancient clay tablets show brewing recipes

questions.text: Name the 4 Teletubbies plus their vacuum cleaner companion.
questions.funfact: The Teletubbies Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa, and Po debuted on BBC in 1997. Noo-noo was the robotic vacuum cleaner who lived with them in the Tubbytronic Superdome.

questions.text: Who has won the most Grammy Awards out of the following - Beyoncé, Taylor Swift, Adele, or Billie Eilish?
questions.funfact: Beyoncé holds the record for the most Grammy wins of all time with 32 awards. Taylor Swift has 14, Adele has 16, and Billie Eilish has 9.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 words — My mama don't like you and she likes everyone / And I never like to admit that I was wrong / And I've been so caught up in my job, didn't see what's going on / But now I know, I'm ___'
acceptedAnswers: better off sleeping on my own
questions.funfact: The lyrics are from Love Yourself by Justin Bieber, written by Ed Sheeran and released in 2015. Ed Sheeran originally wrote it as a diss track but felt it was too mean to release himself.

questions.text: Is colour-blindness more prevalent in men or women?
questions.funfact: Colour blindness affects around 1 in 12 men (8%) but only 1 in 200 women (0.5%). This is because the most common form is caused by a recessive gene on the X chromosome, men only have one X chromosome, so one faulty copy is enough, while women need two faulty copies to be affected.

questions.text: Which is the most valuable company on the NASDAQ by market cap since June 2024?
questions.funfact: Nvidia overtook Apple to become the most valuable company on the NASDAQ with a market cap of around $4.8 trillion, driven by huge growth in AI.

questions.text: Which came first — Charlie Chaplins birth or Count Draculas first appearance?
questions.funfact: Charlie Chaplin was born on 16 April 1889, while Count Dracula first appeared in Bram Stoker's novel in May 1897 making Chaplin about 8 years older than the fictional vampire.

questions.text: What happened in Britain on September 12th, 1752?
options: The Great Fire of London began
questions.funfact: September 12th 1752 never existed in Britain. When switching from the Julian to the Gregorian calendar, 11 days were skipped people went to sleep on September 2nd and woke up on September 14th.

questions.text: What does the word 'undulating' mean?
questions.funfact: Undulating means wave like, often used to describe greens in golf when they look hilly and like the sea waves.

questions.text: What word follows BLUE, follows SPERM, and comes before SHARK to make three new words?
questions.funfact: Blue Whale, Sperm Whale, and Whale Shark — three of the ocean's most iconic giants connected by one word. The blue whale is the largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth.

questions.text: Who has scored more World Cup goals — Messi across 6 tournaments or Scotland as a team across 9 tournaments?
questions.funfact: Messi has scored 21 World Cup goals across 6 tournaments. Scotland have scored 22 goals as a team across 9 World Cups — but have never made it past the group stage.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Wes for this question!

questions.text: After matching online, Astrid (32) meets Ed who says: 'I'm really the same age as you… plus half my age.' How old is Ed?
questions.funfact: If Ed is 32 + half his age, then half his age = 32, so his full age = 64. He's twice Astrid's age which explains why he looked twice as old as his photo

questions.text: The line 'Ugh, as if!' is most associated with which film?
questions.funfact: The line is delivered by Cher Horowitz, played by Alicia Silverstone, in the 1995 cult classic Clueless. The film is a modern retelling of Jane Austen's Emma, set in Beverly Hills.

questions.text: Who is the men's singles champion of Wimbledon 2026?
questions.funfact: Jannik Sinner is the back to back Wimbledon champion and current world No. 1 in 2026. Carlos Alcaraz is currently absent due to a wrist injury.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a greeting in German?
questions.funfact: Treppenwitz translates as Staircase - wit, the frustrating moment you think of a perfect comeback too late. The German greetings are Guten Morgen (good morning), Hallo (hello), and Guten Tag (good day).

questions.text: Which stadium has the largest capacity — Nou Camp, Wembley, Croke Park or MetLife?
questions.funfact: The Nou Camp (Camp Nou) in Barcelona tops the list at 99,354 capacity, ahead of Wembley in London (90,000), MetLife in New Jersey (82,500), and Croke Park in Dublin (82,300). Camp Nou is currently being renovated and will expand to 105,000 when complete.

questions.text: Unscramble this animal anagram: MEUBE BLEB
questions.funfact: Bumblebees are among the most important pollinators on the planet. Unlike honeybees, they don't store large amounts of honey and can sting multiple times — though they rarely do.

questions.text: Hawaiian pizza was actually invented by a Greek man in which country?
questions.funfact: Hawaiian pizza was invented by Sam Panopoulos, a Greek immigrant, at his restaurant in Chatham, Ontario, Canada in 1962. He added canned pineapple to pizza on a whim — and sparked a debate that continues to this day.

questions.text: Which celebrity couple were known as 'Bennifer'?
questions.funfact: Bennifer refers to Ben Affleck and Jennifer Lopez, who first dated from 2002–2004 before rekindling their romance in 2021 and marrying in 2022. Their original relationship was one of the most talked-about celebrity stories of the early 2000s.

questions.text: Which cloud type reaches the highest altitude — cumulus, cirrus or stratus?
questions.funfact: Cirrus clouds form at altitudes between 6,000 and 12,000 metres — the highest of the three. They're made of ice crystals and appear as thin, wispy streaks. Stratus clouds sit lowest, often below 2,000 metres.

questions.text: Which country has the only national flag in the world that is not rectangular or square?
questions.funfact: Nepal's flag consists of two stacked triangular pennants, making it the only non-quadrilateral national flag in the world. The crimson red and blue border are traditional Nepalese colours, and the symbols represent the Himalayan mountains and Hindu and Buddhist religions.

questions.text: In what year did Spotlight win the Oscar for Best Picture, the UK vote for Brexit happen and Donald Trump was elected US President for the first time?
questions.funfact: 2016 was one of the most eventful years in recent history — Spotlight's shock Best Picture win over The Revenant, the UK's Brexit referendum vote in June, and Donald Trump defeating Hillary Clinton in November.

questions.text: In the acronym PTSD, what does the 'T' stand for?
questions.funfact: PTSD stands for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, a mental health condition triggered by experiencing or witnessing a terrifying event. It was first formally recognised as a diagnosis in 1980, though it was known previously as 'shell shock' in World War I veterans.

questions.text: The phrase 'the cat's meow' means someone or something is outstanding — but which decade did this slang originate?
questions.funfact: The cat's meow originated in the 1920s as part of a wave of animal-themed slang like 'the bee's knees' and 'the cat's pajamas.' It was popularised by cartoonist Thomas A. Dorgan and became synonymous with the flapper era.

questions.text: Who founded the Mormon religion (The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints)?
questions.funfact: Joseph Smith founded the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in 1830 in upstate New York. He claimed to have received golden plates from an angel named Moroni, which he translated into the Book of Mormon.

questions.text: Put these leaders in chronological order — who came THIRD: Genghis Khan, Alexander the Great, Napoleon, Mao Zedong?
questions.funfact: The correct order is Alexander the Great (356–323 BC), Genghis Khan (1162–1227), Napoleon (1769–1821), and Mao Zedong (1893–1976). Napoleon comes third, having built his empire more than 500 years after Genghis Khan.

questions.text: Name the top 5 most common food allergies in the world, excluding nuts and peanuts. (I want the foods, not the allergy name!)
questions.funfact: The big 9 allergens recognised globally are milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans, and sesame. Milk and egg allergies are the most common in children, while shellfish allergies are the most prevalent in adults.

questions.text: What was Nirvana's 1991 album called, featuring Smells Like Teen Spirit and Come as You Are?
questions.funfact: Nevermind was released in September 1991 and became one of the best-selling albums of all time, with over 30 million copies sold. Its release is widely credited with bringing grunge and alternative rock into the mainstream.

questions.text: Complete the next 2 words — 'You call me up again just to break me like a promise / So casually cruel in the name of ___ ___ '
questions.funfact: The lyrics are from All Too Well (10 Minute Version) by Taylor Swift, released on the Red (Taylor's Version) album in 2021. The song is widely considered one of her greatest works and is believed to be about her relationship with Jake Gyllenhaal.

questions.text: What whale is known as the 'unicorn of the sea', famous for its long spiral tusk?
questions.funfact: The narwhal's iconic tusk is actually an elongated tooth that can grow up to 3 metres long. Only males typically grow them, and they're found in the cold Arctic waters of Canada, Greenland, Norway and Russia.

questions.text: The Starbucks brand name is a reference to a character in which classic novel?
options: The Old Man and the Sea
questions.funfact: Starbucks is named after Starbuck, the first mate in Herman Melville's 1851 novel Moby Dick. The founders chose a nautical theme to evoke the seafaring history of early coffee traders — the original name considered was 'Pequod', the name of the ship.

questions.text: What does the word 'Sahara' actually mean in Arabic?
questions.funfact: Sahara literally means 'desert' in Arabic — so calling it the 'Sahara Desert' is technically saying 'Desert Desert.' The same applies to the Gobi — it means 'desert' in Mongolian. Many famous geographical names are actually just descriptions in their original language.

questions.text: Which of these capitals is the most northern: Berlin, Amsterdam, London?
questions.funfact: Amsterdam is the northernmost, followed by Berlin and then London is the southernmost.

questions.text: What word comes after POCKET, after STOP and before DOG?
questions.funfact: Pocket watch, stopwatch, and watchdog — three compound words connected by one word. The mechanical pocket watch was the dominant timekeeping device for over 400 years before the wristwatch took over in the early 20th century.

questions.text: A BLUEBERRY PIE costs $12, a CHERRY PIE costs $9, a LEMON PIE costs $8. How much does a STRAWBERRY PIE cost?
questions.funfact: You charge $1 per letter. Strawberry Pie has 13 letters (S-T-R-A-W-B-E-R-R-Y-P-I-E), so it costs $13. Blueberry Pie = 12, Cherry Pie = 9, Lemon Pie = 8 all check out!

questions.text: Who is the world No. 1 ranked chess player in 2026 and has been Number 1 since 2011?
questions.funfact: Magnus Carlsen of Norway holds the No. 1 FIDE rating with 2840 — almost 50 points clear of second-placed Hikaru Nakamura. Interestingly, Gukesh Dommaraju is the current World Chess Champion, but the champion and the top-rated player are different things in chess.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Paul for this question!

questions.text: If A = 1, B = 2 all the way up to Z = 26. What country is represented by 19161914?
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Graeme for this question!

questions.text: In Dirty Dancing, Patrick Swayze's character says Nobody puts ___ in a corner — what name completes the line?
questions.funfact: The line is delivered by Johnny Castle (Patrick Swayze) in the 1987 film Dirty Dancing. Jennifer Grey plays Frances 'Baby' Houseman. The film cost $6 million to make and grossed over $214 million worldwide.

questions.text: Who has just won the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.funfact: Spain has just won their second World Cup title at the 2026 tournament, only conceding one goal the whole tournament.

questions.text: Which country has the largest population of Spanish speakers in the world?
questions.funfact: Mexico has over 120 million Spanish speakers — the most of any country in the world. While Spanish originated in Spain, the language spread throughout the Americas during colonisation and is now spoken by over 500 million people globally.

questions.text: Which tennis Grand Slam attracts the highest global TV viewership?
questions.funfact: Wimbledon consistently draws the highest global TV audience of all four Grand Slams, with an estimated 1 billion viewers in over 200 countries. Its grass courts, royal traditions and iconic Centre Court make it the most prestigious and watched tennis event in the world.

questions.text: Unscramble this anagram to find a flower: FELONRSUW
questions.funfact: Sunflowers are famous for a phenomenon called heliotropism — their stems track the sun from east to west during the day. Once they mature, they stop moving and permanently face east to attract pollinating insects in the morning warmth.

questions.text: What colour were carrots originally before being cultivated into the orange variety we know today?
questions.funfact: Wild carrots were originally purple and white. The orange carrot was selectively bred in the Netherlands in the 17th century, possibly as a tribute to the Dutch royal House of Orange. Purple, yellow and white heirloom varieties still exist today.

questions.text: Which actor has played a villain in the DC Universe, an antihero in the Marvel Universe, and a villain in Blade Runner franchise too?
questions.funfact: Leto has played Joker (villain) in Suicide Squad, Morbius in the Marvel franchise, and Niander Wallace in Blade Runner 2049

questions.text: What type of animal was Laika, the first living creature to orbit Earth in 1957?
questions.funfact: Laika was a stray dog from Moscow who was launched into orbit aboard the Soviet spacecraft Sputnik 2 in November 1957. Sadly, Laika did not survive the mission — the technology to return safely to Earth had not yet been developed.

questions.text: Japan's flag is known as the Hinomaru — what does Hinomaru mean?
questions.funfact: Hinomaru means 'circle of the sun' in Japanese. The flag features a bright red circle perfectly centered on a white background. A 1999 law officially standardised the design, moving the red disc to the exact centre of the flag.

questions.text: Brazil won their first FIFA World Cup, the launch of NASA, and Hitchcock's Vertigo was released — what year?
questions.funfact: 1958 was a landmark year — Brazil won their first of five World Cup titles in Sweden with a 17-year-old Pelé scoring twice in the final, Lego patented its iconic interlocking brick design in Denmark, and Hitchcock released Vertigo, now widely considered one of the greatest films ever made.

questions.text: Which is the correct British English of the medical condition involving frequent watery bowel movements?
questions.funfact: Diarrhoea is the British, Australian and New Zealand spelling, while Diarrhea is the American English version. Both spellings come from the Greek 'diarrhoia', meaning 'a flowing through.' It's one of the most commonly misspelled medical words in the English language.

questions.text: If you are acrophobic, what are you afraid of?
questions.funfact: Acrophobia is an extreme fear of heights, affecting around 5% of the population. It comes from the Greek word 'akron' meaning 'peak' or 'summit.' It's one of the most common specific phobias and can trigger panic attacks even at moderate heights.

questions.text: The Heinz brand is famous for its 'Varieties' slogan — but how many varieties are included on every bottle?
questions.funfact: When Henry Heinz coined the '57 Varieties' slogan in 1896, the company already produced over 60 products. Today Heinz makes over 1,000 products worldwide. Henry chose 57 simply because he liked the number — 5 was his lucky number and 7 was his wife's.

questions.text: What was the name of the ancient Stone used to decypher Egyptian Hieroglyphs?
questions.funfact: The Rosetta Stone, carved in 196 BC, contains a decree issued by King Ptolemy V granting tax exemptions to Egyptian priests. It was written in three scripts — Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics, Demotic script, and Ancient Greek — which allowed scholars to finally decode hieroglyphics.

questions.text: Name the top 5 best-selling soft drinks in the world - including energy drinks and excluding diet/ no sugar variations
questions.funfact: Coca-Cola is the undisputed global leader, selling billions of servings daily across 200+ countries. Red Bull, despite being an energy drink rather than a traditional soft drink, outsells almost everything else globally. The top 5 is dominated by just two companies — Coca-Cola and PepsiCo.

questions.text: Which former Beatle narrated Thomas the Tank Engine in the UK?
questions.funfact: Ringo Starr narrated the first two series of Thomas the Tank Engine & Friends from 1984 to 1986. He was replaced by Michael Angelis for the UK version from series 3 onward. Ringo also sang the theme song and introduced each episode.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 words — If you like piña coladas / And gettin' caught in the rain / If you're not into yoga / If ...
questions.funfact: The lyrics are from Escape (The Piña Colada Song) by Rupert Holmes, released in 1979. It was the last number one hit of the 1970s in the US. The song is about a man who answers a personal ad, only to discover it was placed by his own partner.

questions.text: What is the only mammal capable of true sustained flight?
questions.funfact: Bats are the only mammals capable of true powered flight. There are over 1,400 species of bats, making them the second largest order of mammals after rodents. Flying squirrels and colugos glide but cannot truly fly — only bats have evolved true wings.

questions.text: What animal features on the Alfa Romeo car badge?
questions.funfact: The Alfa Romeo badge features a green serpent (or dragon) devouring a human figure on the right side, and the red cross of Milan on the left. The snake design is taken from the coat of arms of the Visconti family, who ruled Milan in the medieval period.

questions.text: True or False — the same person created both Kermit the Frog (Muppets) and Cookie Monster (Sesame Street)?
questions.funfact: True! Jim Henson created the Muppets, including Kermit the Frog, and also created the Muppet characters for Sesame Street — including Cookie Monster. Henson was a puppeteer, filmmaker and director who also created Fraggle Rock and directed The Dark Crystal and Labyrinth.

questions.text: What colour is an airplane's black box flight recorder actually painted?
questions.funfact: Black boxes are actually painted bright orange to make them easier to locate after a crash. They're built to withstand extreme heat, pressure and impact, and emit a sonar ping for up to 30 days when submerged in water. The name black box is thought to date back to early aviation slang.

questions.text: What do you call a group of flamingos?
questions.funfact: A group of Flamingos are a Flamboyance, a Stand or a Colony .

questions.text: What word goes before COLOUR, after WASTE and after UNDER?
questions.funfact: Watercolour (a painting technique), Wastewater (sewage and used water), and Underwater (below the surface) — three compound words connected by one word. Watercolour painting dates back to the Palaeolithic era and cave paintings.

questions.text: Which is the oldest golf course in the world?
options: The Old Course at St Andrews
questions.funfact: The Old Course at St Andrews in Fife, Scotland, has documented play dating back to around 1552 and is universally recognised as the home of golf. Ratho Farm Golf Links in Tasmania (1822) is considered the oldest in the Southern Hemisphere, while Pau Golf Club in France (1856) is the oldest in continental Europe.

questions.text: If a hen and a half lays an egg and a half in a day and a half, how many eggs will half a dozen hens lay in half a dozen days?
questions.funfact: The answer is 24 (two dozen). If you scale up both the hens (1.5 to 6 = ×4) and the days (1.5 to 6 = ×4), the number of eggs scales by 4×4 = 16 times: 1.5 × 16 = 24.

questions.text: Which M. Night Shyamalan movie contains the line 'I see dead people'?
questions.funfact: The line is delivered by Haley Joel Osment's character Cole Sear in the 1999 film, one of the most quoted movie lines of that decade.

questions.text: In New York, the area where musicals are staged is called Broadway. What is the equivalent theatre district in London called?
questions.funfact: The West End is home to over 40 theatres, some dating back to the 17th century.

questions.text: In the Guggenheim Museum, what piece of fruit has been duct-taped to the wall as a famous artwork?
questions.funfact: The artwork is 'Comedian' a piece consisting of a fresh banana duct-taped to a wall exactly 1.6 metres above the floor and has even been eaten on occasion.

questions.text: How many legs does a scorpion have, excluding pincers and tail?
questions.funfact: Scorpions are arachnids, like spiders, which is why they have 8 legs rather than 6 like insects.

questions.text: Unscramble this animal: CDOLEIROC
questions.funfact: Crocodiles have been around for over 200 million years, older than many dinosaurs.

questions.text: Which music icon was known as 'The Man in Black'?
questions.funfact: Cash said he wore black in solidarity with the poor, prisoners, and victims of war.

questions.text: What does IQ stand for?
questions.funfact: The term was coined by psychologist William Stern in 1912, originally calculated as mental age divided by chronological age, multiplied by 100.

questions.text: How many rings are in the Audi logo?
questions.funfact: The four rings represent the 1932 merger of four German car manufacturers: Audi, DKW, Horch and Wanderer.

questions.text: In what year did Nelson Mandela become President of South Africa, did the Channel Tunnel between England and France open, and did Friends premiere on NBC?
Which one of these flags contains white: Jamaica, Sri Lanka, South Africa, or Germany?
questions.funfact: South Africa's flag has white bands, while Jamaica's (black, yellow, green) and Germany's (black, red, golden yellow) and Sri Lanka's (maroon, golden yellow, orange, and green) don't.

questions.text: Which part of the body uses the most energy?
questions.funfact: The brain makes up about 2% of body weight but uses roughly 20% of the body's energy.

questions.text: What do you call the point of no return for a black hole?
questions.funfact: Not even light can escape once it crosses the event horizon, which is why black holes appear completely black.

questions.text: Who wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?
questions.funfact: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, an Oxford maths lecturer who wrote the story for a young girl named Alice Liddell.

questions.text: In which language does 'Wibli Wobli' mean jellyfish?
questions.funfact: It's a playful, informal nickname, 'pysgod wibli wobli' literally translates to 'wibbly wobbly fish.'

questions.text: Name the 5 boroughs of New York City.
questions.funfact: New York City became a five-borough city in 1898 when Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Staten Island were consolidated into one municipality.

questions.text: What do you call the flighted object in badminton?
questions.funfact: A shuttlecock can decelerate faster than almost any other object in sport, smash shots can leave the racket at over 300 mph but slow dramatically due to its drag.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics — 'Just a small town girl / Livin' in a lonely world / She took the midnight train going anywhere / Just a city boy / Born...'
questions.funfact: Released in 1981, the song became a streaming-era phenomenon and is the best-selling digital track from the 20th century in the US.

questions.text: What is the singular for the word 'data'?
questions.funfact: 'Data' is technically the plural of the Latin 'datum,' though in modern English it's almost always treated as an uncountable noun on its own.

questions.text: How many Stations of the Cross are there in relation to catholicism?
questions.funfact: The Stations of the Cross trace Jesus's final hours, from his condemnation to his burial, and are traditionally displayed around the walls of Catholic churches.

questions.text: Which typically has more calories — a glass of wine or a pint of beer?
questions.funfact: A standard pint of beer runs roughly 180-210 kcal versus about 130-165 kcal for a standard glass of wine, though it varies with ABV and pour size.

questions.text: A child wants to write a coded letter to Santa and they asks for the following: C_E N_P F_H. What is the child asking Santa for?
questions.funfact: If you take gaps between the letters c_e, n_p, f_h - you end up with D - O - G

questions.text: Which person is the odd one out — Steve Jobs, Elizabeth Taylor, Sabrina Carpenter, Tim Cook?
questions.funfact: The other three share surnames that are all trades or careers — Taylor, Carpenter and Cook.

questions.text: What word goes before 'man' and 'code', and after 'goal'?
questions.funfact: Postman, postcode, goalpost.

questions.text: Ouagadougou is the capital of which African country?
questions.funfact: Ouagadougou is often nicknamed 'Ouaga' and is Burkina Faso's largest city as well as its capital.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Graeme for this question!

questions.text: What are the chances of 2 dice rolling a combined total of 8?
questions.funfact: The combinations are (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3) and (6,2) — 5 out of 36 possible rolls.

weekly_quizzes.title: Big Fat Sunday Quiz #17
weekly_quizzes.description: This week is all abote Canada - ay! Big Shoutout to Daire for this suggestion for this themed Trivia!

questions.text: Which movie features the line 'Draw me like one of your French girls'?
questions.funfact: Titanic was directed by Canadian filmmaker James Cameron and remains one of the highest-grossing films ever made.

questions.text: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.funfact: Ottawa was chosen as the capital by Queen Victoria in 1857, partly because it sat safely between the rival cities of Toronto and Quebec City.

questions.text: What is the nickname for the Canadian $1 coin?
questions.funfact: It's named after the loon pictured on the coin's design.

questions.text: What does the word 'Inuit' mean?
questions.funfact: The singular form, 'Inuk', simply means 'person'.

questions.text: Unscramble this anagram of a famous Canadian actor: RECIRJMAY
questions.funfact: Carrey was born in Newmarket, Ontario.

questions.text: Poutine is made of chips and cheese curds, plus which third ingredient?
questions.funfact: Poutine originated in rural Quebec in the late 1950s. Its name translates in Quebec as a 'mess' or 'jumble'.

questions.text: Which Canadian star was Borat's love interest in the 2006 film 'Borat'?
questions.funfact: Anderson is from Ladysmith, British Columbia.

questions.text: Insulin, a Canadian invention used to treat diabetes - is it taken to lower high blood sugar, or to raise low blood sugar?
questions.funfact: Insulin is never used to treat low blood sugar - that's treated with fast-acting sugar or glucagon instead.

questions.text: In which year did Canada host the Winter Olympics, Justin Bieber release his hit single 'Baby', and 'Scott Pilgrim vs. the World' hit theatres?
questions.funfact: The 2010 Winter Olympics were held in Vancouver.

questions.text: Which Canadian baseball team made it to the Major League Baseball World Series in 2025?
questions.funfact: The Blue Jays lost a thrilling seven-game series to the Los Angeles Dodgers, with Game 7 decided in extra innings.

questions.text: What does 'Q' stand for in the NATO phonetic alphabet?
questions.funfact: The alphabet was developed in the 1950s with help from Jean-Paul Vinay, a Canadian linguistics professor from the University of Montreal.

questions.text: Which one of the following singers is NOT Canadian?
questions.funfact: Sia is Australian, from Adelaide.

questions.text: Wayne Gretzky, who wore #99, is considered the best NHL player of all time - what was his nickname?
questions.funfact: "The Iceman" belongs to basketball's George Gervin, "Magic" to Earvin Johnson, and "The Thorpedo" to swimmer Ian Thorpe.

questions.text: Who invented the telephone?
questions.funfact: Bell lived in Canada and later became a Canadian citizen; he patented the telephone in 1876. Baird invented the television, Watt improved the steam engine, and Hings - a Canadian - invented the walkie-talkie.

questions.text: Name Canada's top 5 recreational winter sports by participation.
questions.funfact: Ice hockey (Hockey) remains Canada's most popular organised winter sport. Lacrosse is the official Canadian summer sport.

questions.text: Which song by The Weeknd, released in November 2019, became the most-streamed song of all time with over 5.5 billion streams?
questions.funfact: The Weeknd (Abel Tesfaye) is from Toronto.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics 'I've heard there was a secret chord / That David played and it pleased the Lord / But you don't really care for music, do ya? / It goes like…' (Format: No punctuation just words!)
questions.funfact: Released in 1981, the song became a streaming-era phenomenon and is the best-selling digital track from the 20th century in the US. Leonard Cohen was born in Montreal, Quebec.

questions.text: Which of these Canadian animals is the SECOND largest by average weight?
questions.funfact: By average weight: Orca (~3,000-6,000 kg) > Moose (~400-700 kg) > Black Bear (~60-300 kg) > Marmot (~3-11 kg).

questions.text: Which Canadian company was once the most dominant mobile phone brand in the USA, and had a 2023 film named after it directed by Candadian director Matt Johnson?
questions.funfact: BlackBerry is headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario.

questions.text: In which Canadian province is French the first language for the majority of the population?
questions.funfact: Quebec is Canada's only province where French is the sole official language.

questions.text: What do you call the outfit of wearing a denim jacket with denim jeans?
What word comes before 'book' and 'base', and follows 'back', to form three new words?
Which Canadian filmmaker has been announced to direct the next James Bond film?
questions.funfact: Villeneuve, known for Dune and Arrival, was announced by Amazon MGM Studios in June 2025.

questions.text: Canada has the largest coastline by far in the world, which country has the second-largest coastline?
questions.funfact: Canada has the longest coastline at 202,080 km, followed by Norway at 83,281 km.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Talisia for this question!

questions.text: Write one trillion as a number. (Format: No commas)
Which movie features the line 'Carpe diem. Seize the day, boys. Make your lives extraordinary'?
questions.funfact: Released in 1989 and starring Robin Williams as English teacher John Keating.

questions.text: The latest Spider-Man movie just had the biggest box office opening weekend of all time. Finish the name: Spider-Man: ___ ___ ___
questions.funfact: It surpassed Avengers: Endgame's long-standing domestic opening record, debuting with $360 million.

questions.text: What is a 'Luddite'?
options: A member of a political party
questions.funfact: Named after Ned Ludd, whose followers destroyed textile machinery in 19th century England.

questions.text: On what day of the year does Mexico celebrate Cinco de Mayo?
questions.funfact: It commemorates Mexico's victory over French forces at the Battle of Puebla in 1862, and is actually celebrated more widely in the USA than in most of Mexico.

questions.text: Unscramble this sport anagram: SEATBELTNIN
questions.funfact: Table tennis became an official Olympic sport at the 1988 Seoul Games.

questions.text: What day of the week is Chick-fil-A famously closed on?
questions.funfact: Founder S. Truett Cathy closed the very first restaurant on Sundays in 1946 so staff could rest and worship, and the policy has stuck ever since.

questions.text: What is the name of Taylor Swift's newlywed husband?
questions.funfact: Kelce is a tight end for the Kansas City Chiefs, and the couple's relationship has been credited with a measurable ratings boost for NFL broadcasts.

questions.text: What breed of Japanese hunting dog is the face of the Doge meme and Dogecoin?
questions.funfact: The meme is based on Kabosu, a Shiba Inu from Japan.

questions.text: Which capital city is the most northern in the world?
questions.funfact: Nuuk (Greenland) sits slightly further north, but Greenland is a territory rather than a sovereign state, so Reykjavik holds the title among independent countries.

questions.text: In which year was Frozen released, did Macklemore release 'Thrift Shop', and did Edward Snowden's NSA leaks happen?
questions.funfact: Frozen went on to become the highest-grossing animated film of all time at that point, a record it held for years.

questions.text: The ACL a ligament in the knee, what does the 'A' stand for?
questions.funfact: The ACL is one of the most commonly injured ligaments in sport, especially in football, basketball, and skiing.

questions.text: Finish the saying: 'Even a broken clock is right...'
questions.funfact: The idiom is often used to suggest that even unreliable sources can occasionally be correct by pure chance.

questions.text: What berry is used to flavour gin?
questions.funfact: By law, gin must have juniper as its dominant flavour to legally be called gin.

questions.text: Which of these animals has Australia NOT waged an organised eradication campaign nicknamed a 'war' against?
questions.funfact: The most famous is the 1932 Emu War in Western Australia, where soldiers with machine guns failed to control invading emus - the birds are widely said to have 'won'.

questions.text: Name 4 Zendaya movies and 1 Zendaya TV show released or will release in 2026.
questions.funfact: Zendaya became the youngest woman ever to win two lead-actress Emmys, for her role in Euphoria.

questions.text: What was the name of Norah Jones' 2002 debut album, also one of its title tracks?
questions.funfact: It's the second-highest selling album of the 21st century, behind only Adele's 21.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics 'I can be your hero, baby/ I can kiss away the pain/ I will stand by you forever/ You…'
questions.funfact: It became one of Iglesias's biggest crossover hits, topping charts across Europe and the US.

questions.text: What is a group of owls called?
questions.funfact: The term is thought to come from C.S. Lewis's Narnia books, where a parliament of owls appears in 'The Silver Chair'.

questions.text: Which is older: Oxford University or Machu Picchu?
questions.funfact: Teaching at Oxford dates back to at least 1096, while Machu Picchu wasn't built until around 1450 - meaning Oxford is nearly 350 years older.

questions.text: Which of these US presidents is the odd one out?
questions.funfact: 3 of them share lend their surnames to titular animated characters. Cleveland (The Cleveland Show), Arthur (the PBS aardvark), and Garfield (the cartoon cat).

questions.text: Which country has the most pyramids in the world?
questions.funfact: Sudan has around 255 pyramids, nearly double Egypt's 138 - built by the ancient Kingdom of Kush, though they're much smaller and steeper than Egypt's.

questions.text: What word can precede 'fish' and 'walk', and follow 'copy', to form three new words?
questions.funfact: Catwalk originally referred to a narrow footway, borrowed from the sure-footed way cats move along ledges.

questions.text: What month is it, given that: last month wasn't May or July; next month isn't January, March, or November; and neither last nor next month is April, August, or December?
questions.funfact: Working through the eliminations by process of exclusion is the fastest way to crack this logic puzzle.

questions.text: What is the name of the famous theorem, unsolved for over 300 years, stating that x^n + y^n = z^n has no positive whole-number solutions for n greater than 2?
questions.funfact: Pierre de Fermat scribbled the claim in a book margin in 1637, saying his proof was too big to fit. It wasn't proven until 1994, by Andrew Wiles.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Tom for this question!

questions.text: If you add up all the whole numbers from 1 to 100, what do you get?
questions.funfact: Legend has it a young Carl Friedrich Gauss solved this instantly by pairing numbers (1+100, 2+99, etc.) instead of adding them one by one.

questions.text: Which movie had the iconic tagline 'In space no one can hear you scream'?
questions.funfact: The tagline was coined for Ridley Scott's Alien (1979) and is regularly ranked among the greatest movie taglines of all time.

questions.text: The UK just held a by-election in Clacton which Nigel Farage won. Who came second at the polls with over 26% of the vote?
questions.funfact: Satirical candidate Count Binface, intergalactic space warrior (real name Jon Harvey) took just over a quarter of the vote in the 2026 Clacton by-election, beaten only by Farage, in what was widely called one of the strangest by-elections in recent UK history.

questions.text: From which alphabet/numeral system does our number system originate?
questions.funfact: The digits 0-9 were actually invented in India, but they're called 'Arabic numerals' because Arab mathematicians introduced them to Europe around the 12th century.

questions.text: In a full Ironman event, how long is the cycle leg in km?
questions.funfact: A full Ironman is a 3.86km swim, a 180.25km (112 mile) bike leg, and a 42.2km marathon run, in that order, with no breaks.

questions.text: Which fruit is this anagram of: TARNINEEC
questions.funfact: Nectarines are genetically almost identical to peaches - the fuzz-free skin comes down to a single recessive gene.

questions.text: If you ask for your martini 'dirty', what are you adding to it?
questions.funfact: The splash of salty olive brine both clouds the drink and gives it a savoury edge - the 'dirtier' the martini, the more brine is added.

questions.text: Who is the youngest child of Kris Jenners family that featured on Keeping Up with the Kardashians?
questions.funfact: Kylie is the youngest of Kris Jenner's six children (Kourtney, Kim, Khloe, Rob, Kendall, Kylie) and became one of the youngest self-made billionaires through Kylie Cosmetics.

questions.text: What 4-letter word is next in the sequence: Kilo, Mega, Giga, ...?
questions.funfact: The metric prefixes climb kilo (10^3), mega (10^6), giga (10^9), tera (10^12), then peta and exa.

questions.text: What two countries make up the Iberian Peninsula?
questions.funfact: The peninsula also contains the tiny nations of Andorra and, arguably, Gibraltar and part of France.

questions.text: In which year did Shakira release 'Hips Don't Lie', did Hannah Montana launch, and was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet?
questions.funfact: 2006 was also the year Twitter launched and Time magazine's Person of the Year was simply 'You', recognising the rise of user-generated content.

questions.text: What does the F in PDF stand for?
questions.funfact: PDF stands for Portable Document Format, created by Adobe co-founder John Warnock and released in 1993.

questions.text: Finish the saying: 'All roads lead to...'
questions.funfact: The phrase reflects how the extensive Roman road network radiated outward from the capital, connecting every province back to the city.

questions.text: What do you call a Mexican wrestler?
questions.funfact: 'Luchador' comes from lucha libre ('free fight'), the Mexican wrestling style famous for colourful masks and acrobatic, high-flying moves.

questions.text: If someone is getting canonised, what are they becoming?
questions.funfact: Canonisation is the formal process by which the Catholic Church officially declares a deceased person to be a saint.

questions.text: Outside of Christianity, name the 5 biggest religions in the world by number of followers.
questions.funfact: Christianity (~2.5bn) and Islam (~1.9bn) together account for over half the world's population; Judaism, despite its prominence, has only ~15 million followers globally.

questions.text: What does the word 'Ska' mean in relation to music?
options: A style of jazz singing where the artist uses nonsense syllables
Walking bass lines, and sharp guitar or piano chords played on the offbeat.
questions.funfact: Ska originated in late-1950s Jamaica, blending mento and calypso with American jazz and R&B, and later evolved into rocksteady and reggae.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics 'When I was a young boy /My father took me into the city…'
questions.funfact: Black Parade tells the story of The Patient, a dying man with cancer, the song use death coming as a childhood memory of a marching band to symbolize the triumph of the human spirit over darkness and the processing of mortality and legacy.

questions.text: If a horse whinnies, what verb describes the noise a sheep makes? (Not 'Baaa'!)
questions.funfact: 'Baa' is the sound itself, while 'bleat' is the verb for the noise a sheep (or goat) makes.

questions.text: Which company produces the most tires in the world per year?
questions.funfact: Lego produces roughly 306 million to 380 million small rubber and polymer tires annually while Michelin produces approximately 180 million to 200 million tyres annually

questions.text: Which one of these is not a primary colour of paints?
questions.funfact: The traditional primary colours are red, blue and yellow - green is a secondary colour, made by mixing blue and yellow.

questions.text: The oldest cow that ever lived was called Big Bertha. How old was she?
questions.funfact: Big Bertha was an Irish cow who died just three months short of her 49th birthday. She also held the Guinness World Record for lifetime breeding with 39 calves, and helped raise £75,000 for charity at parades - where her owner O'Leary reportedly fed her whiskey to steady her nerves.

questions.text: What word can go before 'hold' and 'fly', and after 'fun', to make 3 new words?
questions.funfact: Household, housefly, and funhouse - all built around the same 5-letter word.

questions.text: By dictionary entries, which letter appears least often in major references like the Oxford English Dictionary, making up less than 0.2% of entries?
questions.funfact: Q comes in at roughly 0.20% of entries, just ahead of Z (0.27%), X (0.29%), and V (1.01%).

questions.text: What does 'Uisce Beatha' directly translate to from Irish for whiskey?
questions.funfact: 'Uisce beatha' literally means 'water of life' - Aisling a popular womans name in Ireland translates to a Beuatiful Dream, and Dia Dhuit, an Irish Hello translates as May God be with you!
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Danielle for this question!

questions.text: Which letter is missing from the following sequence: B, C, D, E, G, P, T, Z?
questions.funfact: These are the letters whose names all rhyme with 'ee' when said aloud - Bee, Cee, Dee, Ee, Gee, Pee, Tee, Vee, and Zee (using the American 'zee' pronunciation) - so V slots in between T and Z.

weekly_quizzes.title: Big Fat Sunday Quiz #20
weekly_quizzes.description: Ben's Trivia URL has now been updated to benstrivia.com for your convenience! Good Luck!

questions.text: What was Matthew McConaughey's breakout role, in which he iconically says 'Alright alright alright'?
options: How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days
questions.funfact: McConaughey largely improvised the line on set in Dazed and Confused (1993) - the film only paid him $325 a day, but it launched his entire career.

questions.text: Before Whitney Houston's iconic 1992 version, which country icon originally wrote and sang 'I Will Always Love You' in 1973?
questions.funfact: Dolly wrote the song as a farewell to her business partner Porter Wagoner, and famously turned down an offer from Elvis Presley to record it because his manager wanted half the publishing rights. Dolly Parton passed away this week on the 25th August 2026 at age 80.

questions.text: What animal is the following in Latin: Canis lupus?
questions.funfact: Canis lupus literally translates to 'dog wolf' - domestic dogs are actually classified as a subspecies, Canis lupus familiaris.

questions.text: If you hit Ctrl - Alt - Delete, which of the following is NOT an option?
questions.funfact: The Ctrl+Alt+Delete screen on Windows also offers 'Lock' and 'Change a password' - Settings isn't there, you'd need to open the Start Menu for that. The combo dates back to IBM engineer David Bradley in 1981, who used it to reboot PCs during testing without a full power cycle.

questions.text: Which meal is the following an anagram of: NAGALAS
questions.funfact: The word 'lasagna' comes from the ancient Greek 'laganon', a flat sheet of pasta dough. The layered baked dish we know today developed later in medieval Naples.

questions.text: Vichyssoise is a soup traditionally served chilled. What vegetables is this dish primarily made from?
questions.funfact: Despite its French name, Vichyssoise is widely credited as an American invention - chef Louis Diat said he created it at New York's Ritz-Carlton in 1917, inspired by the leek-and-potato soup his mother made back in France.

questions.text: In what role will Robert Downey Jr. return in the upcoming Avengers movie?
questions.funfact: Downey played Tony Stark/Iron Man for over a decade; he returns to the MCU as the villain Victor von Doom in Avengers: Doomsday, due in theatres December 2026.

questions.text: If you are short-sighted (myopic), which of the following is true?
options: Blurry vision when looking at close items
Blurry vision when looking at far items
questions.funfact: Short-sightedness happens when the eyeball is slightly too long or the cornea too curved, so light focuses in front of the retina instead of directly on it.

questions.text: Only three countries in the world have names starting with the letters O, Q and Y (one each). Name all three, in alphabetical order. (Format: Country 1 Country 2 Country 3)
questions.funfact: Oman is the oldest continuously independent state in the Arab world, ruled by the Al Said dynasty since 1749. Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup - the first ever held in the Middle East. Yemen's capital, Sana'a, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth.

questions.text: Guess the year: 'Don't Go Breaking My Heart' by Elton John & Kiki Dee topped the charts, Martin Scorsese's Taxi Driver hit cinemas, and the US celebrated its Bicentennial (200th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence).
questions.funfact: 1976 was also the year Apple Computer was founded by Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak, and Nadia Comaneci scored gymnastics' first-ever perfect 10 at the Montreal Olympics.

questions.text: What does the H in ADHD stand for?
questions.funfact: ADHD stands for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder - not everyone with ADHD is hyperactive, which is why there are inattentive, hyperactive-impulsive, and combined presentations.

questions.text: In Gen Z slang, the word 'Rizz' (meaning charm, or the ability to attract a romantic partner) originates from which longer word?
questions.funfact: 'Rizz' was Oxford Dictionary's Word of the Year for 2023 - it's a shortened, middle chunk of the word 'charisma'.

questions.text: 2 of the Rock formations in Geology are Sedimentary and Metamorphic - what is the third group of stone called?
questions.funfact: Igneous rock forms when molten magma or lava cools and solidifies - it's behind the hexagonal columns at Devils Tower in Wyoming and Northern Ireland's Giant's Causeway.

questions.text: What gas were blimps, including the Hindenburg, historically filled with?
questions.funfact: The Hindenburg burst into flames and was destroyed in just 34 seconds while attempting to land in New Jersey, in 1937 - modern airships now use non-flammable helium instead.

questions.text: On the TV show Friends, Ross technically had the most screen time of any character. Name the other 5 main characters - first and last name.
questions.funfact: Friends ran for 10 seasons (1994-2004), and by the final two seasons each of the six lead actors reportedly earned $1 million per episode - one of the highest per-episode rates in TV history.

questions.text: What was Radiohead's first album called?
questions.funfact: Pablo Honey was released in 1993 and features the breakout single 'Creep' - a song the band reportedly grew tired of playing live for years afterward.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics: 'Up ahead in the distance, I saw a shimmering light / My head grew heavy and my sight grew dim, I had...'
questions.funfact: These are the opening lyrics to the Eagles' 'Hotel California' - released in 1976, the same year as this quiz's 'Guess the Year' question.

questions.text: If you see an orange cat, is it more likely to be male or female?
questions.funfact: About 80% of orange cats are male. The orange fur gene sits on the X chromosome, so males (XY) need only one copy to be fully orange, while females (XX) need two - one from each parent.

questions.text: Which social media company was originally named Picaboo?
questions.funfact: Snapchat's ghost mascot is officially named Ghostface Chillah, a nod by co-founder Evan Spiegel to Wu-Tang Clan rapper Ghostface Killah.

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a logical fallacy (flawed reasoning)?
questions.funfact: Slippery Slope, Red Herring and Straw Man are all classic named fallacies - 'Rolling the Dice' isn't a recognised fallacy at all, just a phrase for taking a gamble.

questions.text: Which one of these iconic movies/franchises has Tim Curry NOT starred in?
options: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York
questions.funfact: Tim Curry played the hotel concierge in Home Alone 2, Pennywise in the 1990 IT miniseries, and Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Picture Show - but he had no role in 2000's How the Grinch Stole Christmas.

questions.text: What word comes before 'way' and 'mark', and after 'town'?
questions.funfact: Hallway, hallmark, and town hall - all built around the same 4-letter word.

questions.text: What letter comes next in the sequence: S, U, M, O, T, U, W, E, T, H, F, R, S?
questions.funfact: The sequence spells out the first letters of the days of the week in order - Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday , so the next letter is A.

questions.text: In what part of the body would you find the 'weenus'?
questions.funfact: The skin on the elbow (the weenus) has very few pain receptors, which is why you can usually pinch or pull it without feeling much.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Jack and Emily for this question!

questions.text: Which of the following means the value that appears most often in a set of data?
questions.funfact: Mode is the most frequent value, Mean is the average, and Median is the middle value when data is ordered - 'Mediocre' isn't a statistical term at all!

questions.text: What movie opens with the following quote from a Narrator: 'This is a story of boy meets girl, but you should know upfront, this is not a love story.'
questions.funfact: (500) Days of Summer's non-linear structure (jumping between days 1 and 488) was inspired by writer Scott Neustadter's own breakup - Zooey Deschanel's Summer was deliberately written as neither villain nor 'dream girl', which is exactly why that opening narration warns you it isn't a love story.

questions.text: Who is the World Number 1 Golfer who just won the PGA Tour Championship and been world #1 for over 3 years?
questions.funfact: Scheffler's 2026 win was his second FedExCup in three years, putting him alongside Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy as the only players with multiple FedExCup titles.

questions.text: If you were to say 'Obrigado' to someone, in what language are you speaking?
questions.funfact: Obrigado literally means 'obliged' - and it's gendered: men traditionally say 'obrigado', while women say 'obrigada'.

questions.text: What was the Bubonic Plague more commonly known as in history, wiping out approximately 30% of Europeans in the 1300's?
questions.funfact: The Black Death killed an estimated one-third of Europe's population between 1347 and 1351, spread mainly by fleas living on black rats aboard trading ships.

questions.text: What country is this an anagram of: NILERORE SEA
questions.funfact: Sierra Leone's capital, Freetown, was founded in 1792 as a settlement for freed and formerly enslaved people.

questions.text: What is the garnish for an espresso martini?
questions.funfact: Traditionally it's 3 coffee beans on top, said to represent health, wealth and happiness. The cocktail was invented by London bartender Dick Bradsell in the late 1980s.

questions.text: Prince William and Kate Middleton have 3 kids together, George and Charlotte are two of them. What is the name of the youngest child?
questions.funfact: Louis was born on 23 April 2018 - St George's Day - and his full name is Louis Arthur Charles.

questions.text: Which one of these has the longest wavelength?
questions.funfact: On the electromagnetic spectrum, radio waves can stretch for kilometres, while X-rays are measured in trillionths of a metre - wavelength and energy move in opposite directions.

questions.text: Which continent has the most countries?
questions.funfact: Africa has 54 UN-recognised countries, 48 to 49 countries for Asia, 44 for Europe and just 12 for South America.

questions.text: Guess the year: Bill Clinton was elected president, A Few Good Men was released in cinemas starring Tom Cruise, and 'Under the Bridge' was released by Red Hot Chili Peppers.
questions.funfact: 1992 was also the year of the Barcelona Olympics, where the USA 'Dream Team' - featuring Michael Jordan, Magic Johnson and Larry Bird - played Olympic basketball together for the first time.

questions.text: What does the M in MRI stand for?
questions.funfact: MRI stands for Magnetic Resonance Imaging - it uses powerful magnets and radio waves rather than radiation, unlike an X-ray or CT (computed tomography) scan.

questions.text: Finish the idiom or saying - 'Don't throw the baby out with the ……'
questions.funfact: The idiom traces back to a German proverb, 'das Kind mit dem Bade ausschütten', first recorded in English in the 1850s by writer Thomas Carlyle.

questions.text: Which of these is FALSE related to leap years?
options: A person whose birthday is on Feb 29th is called a Leapling
Bachelor's Day: an old European tradition where women are allowed to propose marriage to men on this day
The year 2100 will be a leap year
People on a fixed monthly salary technically work an extra day for free in a leap year
questions.funfact: The Gregorian calendar skips leap years in century years not divisible by 400 - so 1900 and 2100 aren't leap years, but 2000 was. It's what keeps our calendar in step with the solar year.

questions.text: Which country gifted the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.funfact: Designed by sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi and dedicated in 1886, the statue's internal iron framework was engineered by Gustave Eiffel - a few years before he built his famous tower.

questions.text: Name the 5 disciplines of the Modern Pentathlon in the Olympics
questions.funfact: The Modern Pentathlon was invented by Baron Pierre de Coubertin for the 1912 Stockholm Olympics to simulate the skills of a 19th-century cavalry soldier behind enemy lines. Equestrian show jumping was dropped after a controversy at Tokyo 2020 and is being replaced by an obstacle course event, like a Ninja Warrior style event from LA 2028 Olympics onwards.

questions.text: Which of the following musicians was NOT blind?
questions.funfact: Beethoven lost his hearing, not his sight - he composed some of his most famous works, including his 9th Symphony, after going almost completely deaf.

questions.text: Complete the next 5 lyrics: 'If you wanna be my lover/ You gotta get with my friends (Gotta get with my friends)/ Make it last forever, Friendship never ends/ If you wanna be my lover….'
questions.funfact: The famous nicknames for the Spice Girls were not chosen by the band or their management, but were instead invented by a magazine editor during a photo shoot because he kept forgetting their names - Posh, Scary, Baby, Ginger, and Sporty.

questions.text: Which of the following animals can't swim?
questions.funfact: Unlike their aquatic turtle relatives, most land tortoises can't swim and can drown if left in deep water too long - they lack the flippers and streamlined shell turtles have.

questions.text: Which is the biggest selling video game console of all time?
questions.funfact: The PlayStation 2 has sold roughly 160 million units. The Nintendo Switch has now overtaken the Wii and DS to become Nintendo's best-selling console ever and the second best-selling console of all time - but it still trails the PS2 with 157 million units.

questions.text: Which one is the odd one out: Joaquin Phoenix, Robert Pattinson, Jack Nicholson, Heath Ledger.
questions.funfact: Phoenix, Nicholson and Ledger have all played the Joker on screen (Phoenix and Ledger both won Oscars for it). Pattinson played Batman himself in 2022's The Batman - not the Joker.

questions.text: Cow hitch, Figure 8 and Sheepshank are all types of what?
questions.funfact: The sheepshank is a knot used to temporarily shorten a rope without cutting it

questions.text: What word can mean both a place of worship and the side of your head?
questions.funfact: Both senses come from the Latin 'templum'. The anatomical temple is thought to be named because that's where hair often shows grey ('time's temple') first as people age.

questions.text: What plant do silkworms typically eat?
questions.funfact: Silkworms (Bombyx mori) are so fully domesticated they can no longer survive in the wild - a single cocoon can unravel into one continuous silk thread up to 900 metres long.

questions.text: Which town or city is home to the world's steepest street?
questions.funfact: Dunedin's Baldwin Street was briefly dethroned by a street in Wales in 2019, but Guinness World Records reinstated it as the world's steepest street in 2020 after a dispute over how the measurement was taken.
questions.shoutout: 🎉 Shoutout to Dannielle for this question!

questions.text: Multiply the number of thumbs that everyone in the world has. What is the result?
questions.funfact: The answer is 0, because at least one person in the world doesn't have thumbs - and anything multiplied by zero is zero.
